# Subtasks

Math items come from subtasks (identifying numbers, counting, comparing,
adding, subtracting, multiplying, number lines, missing numbers and
fractions). The adaptive form chooses items by difficulty, so which
subtasks a child sees depends on their ability.

```{r math-trials}
math <- trials |>
  mutate(subtask = item_group,
         age_band = cut(age_at_run(run_id), c(3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 16), right = FALSE,
                        labels = c("3–4", "5–6", "7–8", "9–10", "11+")),
         form = if_else(adaptive, "adaptive", "fixed")) |>
  filter(!is.na(age_band), !is.na(subtask))
```

```{r math-subtask-accuracy, fig.height=5}
#| label: fig-math-subtask-accuracy
#| fig-cap: "Accuracy by subtask and age (cells with 50 or more responses)."
math |>
  group_by(subtask, age_band) |>
  summarise(accuracy = mean(correct, na.rm = TRUE), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n >= 50) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age_band, y = reorder(subtask, accuracy), fill = accuracy)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = f2(accuracy), colour = accuracy > .5), size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "black", `FALSE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = NULL)
```

```{r math-routing, fig.height=5}
#| label: fig-math-routing
#| fig-cap: "Share of each age group's responses that come from each subtask, on the adaptive and fixed forms."
math |>
  count(form, age_band, subtask) |>
  group_by(form, age_band) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age_band, y = share, fill = subtask)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(vars(form)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(12, "Paired"))(n_distinct(math$subtask)),
                    name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Share of responses")
```

# Open issues

`r below_chance_issue()`
- Math items differ in difficulty across languages more than most tasks'
  items, plausibly because of curriculum
  ([items across languages](../monitor/languages.qmd)).
- Children under 4 are at or near the bottom of the scale, and the bank
  has few items for them
  ([downward extension](../monitor/downward_extension.qmd#fig-official-by-age)).
- Math scores before registry v1.2 were affected by an item-order scoring
  bug, since fixed
  ([IRT column-order study](../studies/2026-06_irt-column-order-bug/math_eap_vs_ml.qmd)).
